newsitem.title: UK: TREASURIES STEADY IN LONDON TRADE PRE-AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: TREASURIES STEADY IN LONDON TRADE PRE-AUCTION.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were seeing moderate trade in London, although most of it was swap related and clustered at the short end, traders said.
The market was awaiting the U.S. Treasury's auction of $10.0 billion of 30-year bonds later on this session, but it was unlikely to shake prices out of the current consolidation band.

"There's been some nibbling at the short end, and swaps related buying as a hedge," said Bill Westgate, vice president at HSBC Securities in London. "The big moves are over -- we are now going to see the bullishness washing out of the market."
U.S. 30 year long bond at 101-26, yielding 6.48 percent versus 101-25 in Tokyo and 101-28 in New York.

Auctions so far this week of 10-year and three-year paper were relatively well received, but "failed to set the world on fire," according to Andy Cossor, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London.
He said there was limited attraction for investors while the 30-year yield was at 6.48 percent.
"Although interest rates may not be going up in the next couple of months, there's a good chance of an increase before the end of the year," he said.
Westgate said market sentiment switched late last week to unequivocal bullishness -- which means there are fewer investors who have yet to be persuaded to buy Treasuries.
"Now everyone is euphoric, and they've bought, the next thing to do is sell," he said.

Wholesale trade and consumer credit data due at 1400 GMT, and 1900 GMT, were not expected to excite the market. Jobless claims to August 2, due 1230 GMT, were forecast at 307,000 compared with 277,000 previously.
September T-bond futures were at 114-24 in automated trade, unchanged from Wednesday's Chicago settlement.
